Subject: Draft post - the shed at a buddies place (pics go on top, not posting yet)

Two Saturdays at a buddies place and I am still laughing. Also still mad. Both at the same time.

Heres the whole list of what I found in that shed, and I am putting it up top of the pictures because you gotta see the duct tape one with your own eyes.

Power was running to the shed on THREE orange extension cords. Daisy chained. Out a basement window, across the yard, under the deck. And one splice wrapped in DUCT tape. Not electrical tape. Duct. Like you would seal a duct.

A 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. Speaker wire going into the outlet. Speaker wire! And the outlet had a GFCI sticker stuck on the front of it, so it was a GFCI, I guess, if the sticker says so.

The ceiling fan box was hanging on ONE drywall screw. One. I touched it and said a word my apprentices have never heard me say.

Mouse nest in the junction box. The mice were fine. Unbothered. They had a better handle on the situation than anybody who ran that wire.

Somebody had opened that panel door with a sharpie and written SHED - DONT TOUCH with a name I did not recognize. I opened it up and the wife standing there goes "who's that" like I was supposed to know. 26 years, no I dont know who that is. Whoever he was he was cheap and a little proud. Thats most of these guys, including me in 2009.

What I did: trenched 18 inches, ran 12/2 UF, put in a 20 amp GFCI breaker, real boxes, real outlets, fan hung on a brace. Permit pulled like an adult. The invoice was two pizzas and a case of Yuengling so dont get any ideas.

But here is the part I actually want to say. Every one of those cords and that duct tape splice was one bad day away from burning a house down. Not my house. Not his house. Yours. I have stood in a 2am rainstorm with my own tools and mine still got hot enough to matter, and it was MY fault, so imagine what happens when the guy doing it is your buddy with a youtube video and a cash offer.

Power is not a DIY weekend. If somebody wants to rewire your garage or your shed, do not let him. Call a licensed electrician, look up the license, pay him, get the permit. I know its money. Money is cheaper than a house fire, and insurance gets real complicated when nobody can produce a permit.

Youre not saving anything except money, and money is not the same thing as safe.

If youve got a panel with duct tape in it, call somebody whose name is on a license. Thats the whole post. Thats the whole message.
